verdict.rationale: Pipedream's docs say you can write Node.js code at any point of a workflow, including npm packages. Its GitHub README adds that Python, Golang and Bash code can also run, and community users confirm the code-based workflows and the addition of Python support. missing for 10: a dedicated first-party docs page detailing Python code steps (the Python claim rests on the README and community, not step-level docs).

support.subject: As a developer, I can drop into real code (JavaScript or Python) as a step inside a workflow

citations.quote: Pipedream supports writing Node.js v at any point of a workflow. Anything you can do with Node.js, you can do in a workflow. This includes using most of npm's 400,000+ packages.
Pipedream allows you to run any Node.js, Python, Golang, or Bash code. You can import any package from the languages' package managers
you can use pre-built components when you're performing common actions, but you can write custom code when you need to.
Python support and the key/value store is super cool to see.
